abstract: The importance of private equity for euro area firms is increasing, with annual growth rates in assets under management exceeding 10%. Private equity buyouts affect more than just the firms being acquired. Using comprehensive data for Belgium, this column shows that the sales volumes of suppliers grow faster when there is a higher proportion of business with customers backed by private equity. But this advantage is lost during downturns, as investors push for cost savings. Buyouts can also crowd out competitors that depend on the same suppliers. Finally, high leverage implies greater interest rate sensitivity, so private equity buyouts can intensify the transmission of monetary policy to target firms and beyond.

abstract: Debates about tariff evasion have focused on Chinese goods entering the US. This column examines the reverse flow and finds that China’s retaliatory tariffs on imports from the US also induced evasion, especially through the misreporting of US-origin goods as originating from other third countries. Trade data and customs enforcement cases help distinguish origin misreporting from genuine trade diversion. The estimates attribute about 35% of the tariff-induced reduction in recorded imports to underreporting, highlighting the need for stronger country-of-origin verification and showing how tariff evasion can make US–China decoupling appear greater than it actually is.
authors: Huijia Liu, Enze Xie, Linhui Yu, Miaojie Yu
